newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 1.4 billion yuan from 2.319 billion yuan with the 60-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said volume was thin with non-banking financial institutions trading less due to a report by the China Securities newspaper on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the central bank's Shanghai branch had warned provincial brokerages trading in Shanghai not to handle state bank funds looking to move into stocks.
No subsidiary of securities houses and trust and investment companies are allowed to borrow money from banks for trading stocks, the newspaper quoted an official as saying.
The subsidiary brokerage offices are also not permitted to trade stocks for themselves, the official said.

"The warning meant the central bank is tightening control over non-banking financial institutions, in particular their subsidiaries," said one trader. "Market sentiment became cautious on Tuesday after the warning."

"Non-banking financial institutions traded less due to the warning and this depressed turnover on Tuesday," a second trader said. "But in the mid-term, it will not have a strong impact because the warning is just a re-affirmation of old rules."
Traders said they expected the interbank rates to move around the current level in the near term, traders said.
